newsitem.title: USA: U.S. masses weapons for possible Iraq air attack.
newsitem.headline: U.S. masses weapons for possible Iraq air attack.

text.p: A U.S. armada of ships and assault planes closed in on Iraq on Friday ready for a punishing bomb attack to end President Saddam Hussein's defiance of allied patrols of Iraqi air space.

As the carrier Enterpise and its task force sailed from the Adriatic to the Gulf to join the carrier Vinson, Clinton administration officials toned down their rhetoric as Republican opponents questioned the wisdom of President (Bill) Clinton's apparent Iraq attack plan.

"I don't want to get in a word war with Saddam Hussein, but we're going to do whatever it takes to keep him from threatening his neighbours, threatening our pilots, and we're going to enforce the no-fly zone," Clinton said at a campaign stop in California.

Defence Secretary William Perry told reporters that the U.S. forces had "robust rules of engagement" when provoked, but did not repeat his warning issued Wednesday that the U.S. response would be "disproportionate."
Perry dismissed as "totally unacceptable" an Iraqi statement that the basing of the F-117A jets in Kuwait was "an act of war against the state of Iraq."
Republican opposition leaders served notice that any Clinton misstep in Iraq would be a major campaign issue.
Led by vice presidential contender Jack Kemp, Republicans weighed in with complaints that Clinton had not been firm enough in dealing with Iraq and demanded closer consultations before any attack.

The Pentagon sent eight F-117A "stealth" fighters to Kuwait, the same planes that were effective in the Gulf war in eluding Iraqi air defences and pummeling targets in the centre of Baghdad. They are due to arrive late on Friday.
The Army said it is moving two Patriot anti-missile batteries, used as a defence against Iraqi Scud missiles during the 1991 Gulf War, to the Gulf in coming days.
The Enterprise, with an additional 75 warplanes, is expected to pass through the Suez Canal by the weekend. The two carriers have F-14 fighters recently modified to carry accurate laser-guided bombs.
U.S. B-52 bombers are at the British base on the Indian Ocean island of Diego Garcia, within striking distance.
The U.S. moves came after Iraq fired an SA-6 missile at two U.S. jet fighters patroling the no-fly zone over northern Iraq on Wednesday.

The Pentagon said Iraqi forces fired three anti-aircraft missiles into the air over southern Iraq on Thursday, but added that the missiles were apparently fired blindly and came nowhere near U.S. and allied warplanes.

U.S.-Iraqi tensions began rising last week when U.S. planes and ships fired 44 cruise missiles at southern Iraqi air defences in retaliation for an Iraqi military action against a Kurdish faction in the north.
But U.S. officials said they detected no movement of Iraqi forces south toward Kuwait.

Former Secretary of State James Baker, who helped organise the coalition that drove Iraqi forces out of Kuwait in the 1991 Gulf War, offered some advice. He said the United States should now "at least consider military targets in and around Baghdad and Republican Guard units north of the 36th parallel."
"I think they really only understand disproportionate force," Baker told the Senate Armed Services Committee.
